svg.title: WildfireGuardian vehicle unit wiring
svg.desc: Raspberry Pi 4/5 40-pin header wired per the user's printed build manual: three MAX31855 thermocouple amplifiers sharing 3V3 pin 17, GND pin 20, CLK pin 23 and DO pin 21, chip selects GPIO8 pin 24 (plate), GPIO7 pin 26 (housing) and GPIO5 pin 29 (air, software chip select); BNO055 on I2C1 at 0x28 (3V3 pin 1, GND pin 6, SDA pin 3, SCL pin 5); USB thermal camera, radar EVM and GNSS; fused 12 V to 5 V power chain. Not verified on hardware.
svg.text: Pin map from the user's printed build manual (2026-11-17). Not wired or verified on hardware. Header viewed from above, pin 1 top left.
3V3 pin 17 -> VIN x3 (3.3 V part: never 5 V)
K probe taped to the wall
Chip selects, active low. Plate CE0 (spidev0.0), housing CE1 (spidev0.1):
kernel CS. Air GPIO5: SOFTWARE CS, driver opens spidev0.0 with no_cs=True,
drives GPIO5 under a lock shared with plate and housing.
Advice: 10 kOhm pull-up GPIO5 -> 3V3. 10 nF across T+/T-.
MOSI (pin 19) unused: the MAX31855 is read-only.
BNO055 TX -> GPIO15 RXD (pin 10), RX -> GPIO14 TXD
InfiRay P2 Pro thermal camera (thermal), USB 0bda:5830
USB-C plug -> USB-C(f) to USB-A(m) OTG adapter or cable
UVC 256x384 YUYV (same frame as the Topdon TC001)
TI IWR6843AOPEVM radar (radar), stock mmw demo
micro-USB, 5 V from USB (about 2-3 W). Two serial ports enumerate:
Board must be in functional mode (SOP switch), see WIRING.md.
NMEA over USB serial, about 0.2 W; antenna needs sky view
Option: powered USB hub fed from the 5 V buck if the Pi limits USB current.
Power: 12 V accessory socket to Pi
+12 V nominal (9-16 V running; dips to about 6 V while cranking; transients above 24 V possible)
Pi 5: USB-C PD 5.1 V 5 A (27 W class)
do not back-feed 5 V via GPIO pins 2/4 unprotected
GND / 0 V: returns through the socket plug only. Copper disc and thermocouple sheaths stay isolated from chassis.
(a grounded junction makes the MAX31855 report SHORT_GND)
CS plate, CE0 GPIO8 pin 24 (blue, dashed)
CS housing, CE1 GPIO7 pin 26 (purple, dashed)
CS air GPIO5 pin 29, software (brown, dashed)
